newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen heading lower again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen heading lower again.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures are likely to continue to drift lower with the key September contract gearing up for a downside target at $1,500 a tonne, technical analysts said on Monday.

Traders called the market to gap $90 down after a sharp fall in New York on Friday following the U.S. Department of Agriculture's higher-than-expected forecast for world and Brazilian coffee production.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said coffee was making an attempt to rally but added that the chances of maintaining the run-up were slim.
Resistance is seen at Friday's high of $1,845 a tonne, basis September but the real hurdle was pegged above $2,000.
"I suspect the downside target is $1,500," she added.
Traders from Brazil to Indonesia have attacked the USDA estimates, released on Friday, which differed greatly from other forecasts.
The USDA said it forecast Brazilian 1997/98 coffee output at 28 million 60-kg bags, up from 27.5 million in 1996/97.
It also said world coffee production in 1997/98 should reach 103.7 million bags against 100.7 million in 1996/97/
Brazilian traders were stunned by the 1997/98 USDA estimate, not so much because of its size but because it put the crop currently being harvested above last year's.
"The USDA will lose its credibility with a report like this", said Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters.
Broker GNI said from the market perspective, it would be surprising if the report was anything but bearish.
"The specs and funds will probably continue with their recent selling -- after all there is no frost-threatening cold front (in Brazil) in prospect for the foreseeable future," it said.
